```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's core deliverable is fully digital, so the brief's own evidence suggests a solo founder with AI agents can build and ship it. A's case against says the hard parts (sourcing, warehousing, customs, breakage, address failures) are physical-logistics problems that AI agents don't solve.",
    "B has several publicly listed, low-ticket price anchors a solo seller could plausibly match for a first sale: Foray at $60 per blueprint or $299/mo, MarketGeist at $49/mo, and Gixo at $10/mo. A's brief says its category sells on enterprise terms (Sendoso at $15k-$20k+/yr), which fits poorly with one person closing a customer in 90 days.",
    "A's undercutting thesis is weak on its own evidence. SwagUp already offers a self-serve $99/mo plan ($80/mo billed annually), and every named competitor already advertises event-triggered swag. That leaves only a thin niche, and buyers would still owe $30-75 per kit on top of any subscription.",
    "A's key feasibility claim, that a no-inventory swag-fulfillment API exists to wire into a Stripe webhook, carries no source in the brief. It therefore counts as missing evidence.",
    "Both ideas face saturated competition. B's main weakness is unit economics: about $104 cost per lead from Google Ads against a roughly $60 product. That is a solvable go-to-market problem, since the brief names organic channels such as Indie Hackers and LinkedIn where the pain is voiced. A's weakness is structural logistics and compliance burden, including ongoing customs handling and GDPR/CCPA address data."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's only quoted demand signal is a LinkedIn commenter who received Stripe's gift and asked which vendor was used. The brief itself concedes the commenter was 'receiving rather than needing to build it.' This is curiosity, not purchase intent, and the 'seed HN quote' it cites is never reproduced.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence; both briefs are thin. B's demand quotes show the pain of deciding between options, not willingness to pay for a tool. The second quote ('Only you can') arguably cuts against a tool, and the risk of users defaulting to a general-purpose LLM is unaddressed. B's competitor pricing validates the category, but some anchors are pre-launch (Insightloop) or missing (PREONZ). B wins mainly because its build and delivery fit a solo AI-agent operator, while A's do not."
}
```
